preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, call setSwapAndLiquifyEnabled(false) to disable the swap and liquify mechanism, effectively stopping automatic liquidity additions and potentially disrupting normal token operations for all users except the owner.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The TeaToken contract has a privileged function setSwapAndLiquifyEnabled() that is only callable by the owner. By becoming the owner (through storage slot manipulation), we can disable the swap and liquify mechanism, which normally automatically adds liquidity from accumulated fees. This disrupts the token's normal operations and could benefit the attacker by preventing automatic selling or liquidity additions.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Overwrite the owner storage slot to make the attacker address the owner. 2. Call setSwapAndLiquifyEnabled(false) as the new owner. 3. Verify that swapAndLiquifyEnabled is now false.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.store() to overwrite the owner storage slot at position 0. 2. Call setSwapAndLiquifyEnabled(false) as the attacker (now owner). 3. Read the swapAndLiquifyEnabled variable to confirm it's false.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The contract has an owner-only function setSwapAndLiquifyEnabled(). We need to call this as the owner to disable the mechanism. Instead of storage manipulation, we can impersonate the current owner.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Get the current owner address by calling the owner() function. 2. Impersonate the owner using vm.prank(). 3. Call setSwapAndLiquifyEnabled(false). 4. Verify the state change.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Call owner() on the contract to get the current owner address. 2. Use vm.startPrank(owner) to impersonate. 3. Call setSwapAndLiquifyEnabled(false). 4. Stop the prank. 5. Verify swapAndLiquifyEnabled is false.
attempts.failure_reflection: The previous approach tried to use vm.store() which might have storage layout issues or RPC rate limiting problems. A simpler approach is to impersonate the existing owner rather than trying to overwrite storage slots.
